level_rationale: Experiencing diarrhea and mild abdominal bloating after drinking milk every day for 4 weeks in a 32-year-old adult meets the 4-week chronic diarrhea threshold requiring an outpatient clinic evaluation to assess malabsorption and exclude organic gastrointestinal disease, whereas having loose stools and mild belly bloating a single time last night after drinking milk is an uncomplicated self-limited dietary upset appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Indian English core dialect lexicon swap ('diarrheal stools and mild abdominal distension' vs 'loose motions and mild belly bloating', keeping 'loose motions' in everyday_paraphrase and changed_fact) + single-fact symptom duration de-escalation control (-cf, every day for 4 weeks to 1 time last night, L2 to L1).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 32, diarrhea after drinking milk, mild abdominal bloating after drinking milk, and daily occurrence for 4 weeks) with an exact 6-word vs 6-word continuous span swap and zero stated negatives. Changing only symptom duration/frequency in fact f4 ('every day for 4 weeks' to '1 time last night') follows Rule A's first-choice duration design and Rule D uniqueness, shifting care cleanly from outpatient clinic chronic diarrhea workup (level 2) to home self-care for a single transient post-milk episode (level 1).
